newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish EGS Bank targets 3 trln lira 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Turkish EGS Bank targets 3 trln lira 1997 profit.

text.p: Turkey's small EGS Bank, owned by some 500 textile producers, manufacturers and exporters, plans to more than triple its 1997 pre-tax profit to three trillion lira from 807 billion in 1996, its general manager said.
"Our aim is to reach a three trillion lira (before-tax) profit in 1997 while raising our total assets to $350 billion from $120 billion in 1996," general manager Ismail Canseven told Reuters.

He said the bank, after securing Treasury approval to become a commercial bank in December 1996, began to accept deposits and doubled the number of its branches in Turkey to 10. Previously, it had worked as an investment bank.
"Our aim is to provide all sorts of financial services to our shareholders and to become a medium-scale bank with 50-60 branches and two billion dollars of assets and a strong equity," Canseven said.
EGS Bank raised its capital 4.4 trillion lira in January from two trillion and part of it was met by 1996 profits. It also plans to add 1997 and 1998 profits onto capital.
"We plan to raise the number of our branches to 24 by the end of this year. The needs of our shareholders are taken into account when opening new branches," he added.
To become a stronger financial group, EGS Bank set up leasing, factoring and insurance firms and a brokerage house besides owning an offshore bank in the Turkish Republic of northern Cyprus.
"We are planning to set up a life insurance company this year and aim to own a bank outside Turkey in 1998-99," said Canseven.

EGS Bank is the first bank in Turkey to be owned by some 500 textile and readywear industrialists and exporters, with each having a capital share of no more than four percent, except readywear exporter EGS Dis Ticaret which holds a 15 percent stake.
